Profile

Phoropter’s pages are its API. A person and an agent read the same HTML; structure is in rel links and microdata (items have no itemtype; property names are defined here). The top-level item in each page’s <main> is the plan, as-built, place, or home listing the page is about.

Link relations

What do the rels and properties on this page mean? This document.
help registered
How are plans written? From every page to the guide, which is the same on every site.
draft phoropter
Is a plan being drafted? From every page to draft/, the repository’s one draft, while plan.draft.md exists. Only the dev server adds it; a built site never has a draft.

collection registered

up registered

as-built phoropter
What changed while this plan was being built? From a plan to its as-built file.
anchored-at phoropter
Where does this entry point? From an anchor on an entry to the page for its symbol or file, or to another plan’s entry, or to a whole plan.
anchored-by phoropter
Which plans point here? From a symbol or file page to each entry anchored there, and from an entry to each entry in another plan whose anchor names it.
revisits phoropter
Whose ground is this plan standing on? From a plan to the one plan its revisits: names (bodkin).
revisited-by phoropter
Has this plan’s ground been revisited? From a plan to each plan that revisits it.
answers phoropter
Which guess does this answer? From an as-built’s Answered: entry to the plan’s Guess: with the same title.
answered-by phoropter
Has this guess been answered? From a plan’s Guess: to the Answered: entry in its as-built.

Microdata properties

(header)
Every page’s provenance, the item in its <header>: repository and commit (full sha in value).
plan
A plan: title, name and date (from its filename), added (the commit that added it, which orders plans), cart as written, base, file, intro, asBuilt, revisits and revisitedBy links, and its entry items. On the home page, a plan has entryCount instead of its entries. When a base (or an as-built’s head) names a commit here, it’s a <data> whose value is the full sha. Otherwise its value is the text as written, like “none, a new repo”, or a commit a squash merge replaced; a missing base is “not given”.
asBuilt
An as-built file: title, plan, head, file, and its entry items.
entry
One entry: kind (Decision, Decline, Guess; in an as-built, Changed, Chose, Answered), title, anchor items, reason, source (the parenthesis after Because or Answer, exactly as written), verdict (an answer’s opening word: held, disproved, partly disproved, or not tested; on a guess, inside its answeredBy link’s sentence), answers or answeredBy links, and anchoredBy links from other plans’ entries.
anchor
Where an entry points: where as written, quote if any, new (content true) for where (new), in the same shape wherever it appears, note when it is shown but not resolved, place (a symbol or file page) or target (another plan’s entry, or a whole plan), and one view per commit. An anchor at an entry has no views unless it has a quote, and then one, at the generated commit: plans and landed as-builts don’t change.
view
An anchor at one commit: role (base, as-built head, generated), commit, status, file, startLine/endLine for a symbol, matches, one match item per match with the startLine and endLine the quote covers, note, code (each one preceded by codeStart, the line number of its first line; the nth codeStart belongs to the nth code), and sameAs when a generated view matches the as-built head’s exactly and its code isn’t repeated. A plan’s anchors have up to three views: base, as-built head (where the plan’s own work landed), and generated.
status
found: the quote matched. not-found: it didn’t. no-quote: nothing to search for. no-file: the file isn’t at that commit. no-symbol: the symbol isn’t in that commit’s index. no-index: the commit couldn’t be indexed for the symbol’s package, so whether it’s there isn’t known; the note names the indexer (batik). None of these judges a difference between commits.
(draft header)
On the draft page, the header says it’s the working tree, not a commit: file (drafts/plan.draft.md), repository, readAt, the draft’s sha256, and the commit its anchors resolve at.
draft
The draft page’s item: title, base, revisits, notesSha256 and annotates (the draft version the notes were written against, when it isn’t this one), intro, entry items as on a plan (but never listed on places or other plans’ entries), prompt items, and annotation items.
prompt
An open question in a draft, in the annotating agreement’s form: kind (Question, Select, Affirm), text, option for each of a Select’s choices, fallback (what happens if it goes unanswered), and answer when the notes restate it. It follows the entry (or intro) it belongs to.
annotation
A note from drafts/plan.draft.notes.md, or, on a landed plan’s page as the dev server serves it, from that plan’s notes in drafts/ (tarlatan): heading as written, quote (the source text it quotes), and comment. It follows the entry whose source holds its quote; a note without a quote, or whose quote isn’t there anymore, comes first. A built site never has a landed plan’s notes.
noteCount
On the home page as the dev server serves it, on a plan with notes in drafts/: how many (tarlatan; organza renamed it from requestCount).
place
A symbol or file that plans anchor to: name, kind, symbol or file, a symbol’s whole definition at the generated commit as code with its codeStart, entryCount on the home page, and anchoredBy items.
